card.name: Words just before route of administration
card.fires_on: Small words like "for", "unintended" or "trans" that come right before a route of administration such as intravenous, intravascular, intrathecal or transdermal, in dosing and administration text.

modes.label: "for" before a route
modes.description: The word "for" after a drug name or reconstituted solution, leading into intravenous or intra-arterial use.

modes.label: Unintended before intravascular
modes.description: "unintended" or "unintentional" just before intravascular or intrathecal injection.
modes.example: This test dose may serve as a warning of<< unintended>> intravascular or intrathecal injection

modes.label: Start of a route word
modes.description: The opening piece of a route word such as transdermal.
modes.example: Rivastigmine transdermal system is a patch for<< trans>>dermal use on intact skin.

card.writes: It seems to push the next word toward a route or setting term rather than the usual continuations; the promoted and suppressed tokens are mixed and unclear.
card.plain: It fires on the little word right before a route of giving a drug, such as intravenous or intravascular.
